DELIBERATE SEQUENCE CHANGE, named: all six seeds moved - 0 (18 lines/220 chars -> 18/220, different words), 1 (40/498 -> 40/495), 7 (14/171 -> 14/174), 42 (11/131 -> 11/132), 1234 (18/233 -> 18/236), 999999 (13/170 -> 13/173). Why: rules.js now multiplies the child-word weights by the parent's word, so pick() lands on a different word from the same random number. The DRAW SEQUENCE is untouched - same count of next() calls per node, same order - which is why gen(seed, {chaos: 1}) is byte-for-byte the pre-rules output: diffed all six seeds against the BEFORE capture, zero differences. Old addresses are reachable as chaos 1, not as #seed.

CORRECTION to the line above - the exact AFTER sizes, read from the captures rather than typed: 0: 18 lines, 220 chars -> 18 lines, 220 chars  (SAME TEXT); 1: 40 lines, 498 chars -> 40 lines, 495 chars; 7: 14 lines, 171 chars -> 14 lines, 171 chars  (SAME TEXT); 42: 11 lines, 131 chars -> 11 lines, 132 chars; 1234: 18 lines, 233 chars -> 18 lines, 232 chars; 999999: 13 lines, 170 chars -> 13 lines, 170 chars  (SAME TEXT). Every one of the six draws a DIFFERENT TREE under the rules even where the size matches; none is bit-identical to its pre-rules text, and all six are bit-identical again at chaos 1.

SEEDS THAT MOVED, computed by comparing the two captures line for line (supersedes the '(SAME TEXT)' label above, which compared SIZES not text): 0: MOVED (18/220 chars -> 18/220); 1: MOVED (40/498 chars -> 40/495); 7: MOVED (14/171 chars -> 14/171); 42: MOVED (11/131 chars -> 11/132); 1234: MOVED (18/233 chars -> 18/232); 999999: MOVED (13/170 chars -> 13/170). The size can match while every word differs - seed 0 is 18 lines both ways and its second child is `list small` now where it was `tabs small`.

TILE CLICK: tile #45 -> url .../generator/#45 and the live tree rebuilt (proof line 'seed 45 - 18 pages, 231 chars, identical on a second run'). TYPED SPEC: typed 5 lines -> tree rebuilt, textarea round-trips the exact text, url becomes #s=wall%20large%0A..., a cold reload of that url rebuilds the same spec and every generated href carries it.

MEASURED TRAP: a config that overrides column() must stamp its own width class - core's column() ends with .ac(this.width && 'page-column-' + this.width), and tree.js does the same. One line fixed it (1675px, eight a row).

assign.outcome:
**Generator wave 2 - a permutation wall, a typed spec, and pairing rules the roller obeys.** All three of v1's cuts, plus the question underneath them.

![the wall at 1920](/framework/ai/2026-08-26/generator-wall/wall-1920.png)

- [Permutation wall](/framework/core/Page/generator/rolls/#42) - 24 rolls at once, each a small picture of its tree, each a link to that seed. `#42` = seeds 42-65; the arrows page the base and the url follows. A tile is a drawing, not 24 mounted page trees.
- [Generator](/framework/core/Page/generator/) - the spec box is a **textarea** now: type a tree and it is built, [addressed by its own text](/framework/core/Page/generator/#s=wall%20large%0A%20%20list%20small%0A%20%20%20%20prose%0A%20%20grid%0Atabs) as `#s=<encoded>`. Round-trip and cold reload verified.
- **Pairing rules** as data in `rules.js` - 8 parent words, a multiplier per child word, a note per row, printed under the tiles so they can be argued with. `gen(seed, {chaos: 1})` ignores them.

**Seed honesty.** The rules change what a seed draws, deliberately: all six proof seeds (0/1/7/42/1234/999999) MOVED - three keep their length and change every word. The draw sequence itself is untouched (same `next()` calls, same order), so `gen(seed, {chaos: 1})` is byte-for-byte the pre-rules output on all six. Both full sets are pasted in this log.

**Verified** headless at 400/1280/1920/3440: **24 tiles, 24 distinct pictures** (the two numbers agree); 2 / 5 / 8 / 15 tiles a row; no horizontal overflow anywhere; a tile click rebuilds that seed's live tree; zero console errors from `generator/**`.

**Trap, measured:** a config that overrides `column()` must stamp its own width class - without it `width: "full"` was a field nobody read and the wall rendered 639px wide, three tiles a row, at 1920.

Docs: [readme](/framework/core/Page/generator/readme/) - [doc/decisions.md](/framework/core/Page/generator/doc/decisions.md) (Wave 2 section).

**Left on purpose:** a chaos dial on the page (it would make `#7` mean two trees); pairing rules for the width words; a wall of typed specs. The dev server was down all session - verification ran against a throwaway static server on 8099, so nothing here has been seen on port 80.

log.msg: REPORTED REGRESSION - diagnosed, and it is NOT a mechanism regression. Cold /generator/tabs/rail/crumbs/#1234 404s because that PATH no longer exists: the pairing rules moved seed 1234, and its third level under 'tabs > rail small' is 'rail' now where it was 'crumbs'. Proved in node: gen(1234, {chaos: 1}) -> 'tabs | rail small | crumbs | prose small' (the wave-1 model, unchanged); gen(1234) -> 'tabs | rail small | rail | prose small'. This is the deliberate sequence change already declared in this log and in doc/decisions.md - a deep generated url is a link into ONE model.

CONTROL TEST on 8093: /generator/zzz/#1234 fails identically - same two resource 404s (the child's page.js and .md probes from Page.child()), same 'Error: 404 - nothing matches' at App.load, same blank page. So the failure mode is core's generic missing-segment 404, not anything wave 2 introduced; wave 1 would have done the same for a stale path.

DEEP COLD LOADS, verified on 8093 at 1920 (the mechanism wave 1 built is intact): /generator/tabs/rail/rail/#1234 -> 4 column bodies, crumbs 'Generator > tabs > rail small > rail', spec 'crumbs full', ZERO console errors (this is the wave-1 url, re-derived for today's model). /generator/rolls/#42 -> 24 tiles, 2 bodies, zero errors. /generator/#s=wall%20large... -> renders the typed tree, spec box holds the typed text. /generator/wall/list/#s=wall%20large... -> 3 bodies, crumbs 'Generator > wall large > list small', zero errors - a DEEP cold load in the new typed-spec address form.

SIX-SEED RE-PROOF after the diagnosis: node capture diffed against the post-wave-2 capture - zero differences. 0/1/7/42/1234/999999 did NOT move again; no code changed to fix this, because there was nothing broken to fix. The only edit is one paragraph in doc/decisions.md naming the casualty: wave 1's /tabs/rail/crumbs/#1234 is dead, the same tree is at /tabs/rail/rail/#1234, and the wave-1 tree is what gen(1234, {chaos: 1}) draws. Rejected as a 'fix': a route() on generated pages that claims unknown child names - it would swallow real 404s to rescue stale links.
